title: Pit loom
summary: A pit loom has its treadles set in a hole in the floor, so the weaver sits at the edge with feet in the pit. Pressing a treadle opens the threads, leaving both hands free to throw the shuttle, and the long narrow strips of cloth that result are sewn side by side into wide cloth.
howToPlay: Pick a thread colour from the cones and a pattern shape from the tray.
Touch a square on the strip to weave that shape there; it is mirrored across and down the strip.
Copy the strip shown on the card, then press Check.
rules: The strip is mirrored both left to right and top to bottom, so each shape is woven on up to four squares.
A square counts only when its shape and its thread colour both match the strip you are copying.
Three stars need a nearly perfect copy; you can undo or clear as often as you like.
heritageNote: Foot-treadle looms set over a pit are found in many dry-climate weaving traditions, where the pit keeps the threads cool and the loom low and steady. They are still used in handloom villages of South Asia and in North Africa.
credits: Pattern design: World Heritage Games (original, in the style of the tradition)
